Explain in 4 short sentences what discrete diffusion language models do.<turn|>
<|turn>model
<|channel>thought
<channel|>Discrete diffusion language models generate text by gradually adding noise to a sequence of tokens until it becomes a set of random symbols. During training, the model learns to reverse this process by predicting the original tokens from the increasingly noisy input. Unlike standard autoregressive models that predict word-by-word, these models refine the entire sequence simultaneously over multiple steps. This approach allows for flexible generation and can better handle global structural constraints within the text.<eos>
answer: Discrete diffusion language models generate text by gradually adding noise to a sequence of tokens until it becomes a set of random symbols. During training, the model learns to reverse this process by predicting the original tokens from the increasingly noisy input. Unlike standard autoregressive models that predict word-by-word, these models refine the entire sequence simultaneously over multiple steps. This approach allows for flexible generation and can better handle global structural constraints within the text.
